title: Tucows Agrees to Sell Ting's Owned Fiber Markets to Clearwave; Expected to Remove $301.5 Million of Securitized Debt at Closing
summary: /CNW/ -- Tucows Inc. (NASDAQ: TCX) (TSX: TC) today announced that its subsidiary Ting Fiber, LLC ("Ting") has entered into a definitive agreement to sell Ting...
body_markdown:
Transaction advances Ting strategic process and Tucows' transition toward a simpler, capital-light portfolio


TORONTO


, Nov. 17, 2026


/CNW/ -- Tucows Inc. (NASDAQ: TCX) (TSX:TC ) today announced that its subsidiary Ting Fiber, LLC ("Ting") has entered into a definitive agreement to sell Ting Holdco LLC ("Ting Holdco"), which holds Ting's owned fiber markets and the securitized financing facility that finances them, to Clearwave, a fiber internet provider backed by GTCR and Berkshire Partners (together, "Clearwave"). Since the securitized debt will remain with Ting Holdco at closing, Tucows expects to remove approximately $301.5 million in principal amount of securitized notes from its consolidated balance sheet. This agreement is a key outcome of the review of strategic alternatives for Ting that Tucows previously announced.


**Transaction highlights**


- **Debt transfers with the business.** Clearwave will acquire Ting Holdco, together with the securitized financing facility, for nominal cash consideration. Based on balances at September 30, 2026, secured notes with a principal of approximately $301.5 million are expected to no longer be reported as debt in Tucows' consolidated financial statements. The notes are non-recourse to Tucows.
- **Tucows contribution.** Tucows will contribute $3.0 million in cash to Simply Bits, LLC, a subsidiary of Ting Holdco, which will remain a subsidiary of Ting Holdco following closing.
- **Funding commitment ends.** Tucows' commitment, under its July 2026 agreement with Ting's former preferred unitholder, to invest up to $12.5 million in Ting will no longer apply.
- **What stays with Tucows.** Ting's partner markets will stay with Tucows and are not part of the transaction.
- **Transition services.** A Tucows subsidiary will provide transition services to Clearwave for nine months after closing, which Clearwave may extend by up to two months
- **One-time costs to Tucows.** Tucows expects to incur one-time costs in connection with the transaction, including advisory fees, cash taxes payable in 2027, a contribution at closing, and employee-related and transition services costs. Most of the taxable gain is expected to be offset by tax loss carryforwards, and Tucows expects to retain tax loss carryforwards after closing.


**Closing and approvals**


The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to a number of conditions, including required approvals from the Federal Communications Commission and state public utility commissions; consents and waivers from securitization noteholders and other parties to the facility; rating agency confirmations; completion of a pre-closing restructuring to cause certain internal asset transfers; the agreement to effect the assignment of the 9.95% Secured Fiber Revenue Notes, Series 2023-1 to Clearwave not being terminated and remaining in full force and effect; certain waivers and confirmations from municipalities and other third parties; and certain other conditions set forth in the purchase agreement.


**Strategic rationale**


The sale is a significant step toward a capital-light, lean operating model. Ting's capital needs have limited Tucows' strategic and financial flexibility for several years. Divesting the owned fiber markets and their securitized debt will leave Tucows able to focus on growing a portfolio of less capital-intensive businesses with recurring revenue, strong customer relationships and scalable platforms.


The agreement builds on steps Tucows took during 2026 to simplify its structure and strengthen its balance sheet, including the retirement of Ting's Series A preferred units in July, the extension of the majority of Tucows' syndicated credit facility to July 2029, and the agreement announced in October to transfer Ting's Colorado Springs network lease, which is expected to be completed in April 2027, at which point Tucows' related parent guaranty will be released.


"This agreement is a key outcome we have been working toward since we began the Ting strategic process," said Dave Woroch, Chief Executive Officer of Tucows. "Upon closing, it is expected to remove more than $300 million in principal amount of securitized debt and the capital demands that came with building fiber networks. What will remain is a simpler, more focused business that we expect to generate cash more consistently: a portfolio of recurring-revenue businesses, led by Tucows Domains and Wavelo, with the flexibility to invest where we see the best returns. Greater flexibility carries an obligation to be disciplined, and Tucows' job now is to put it to work in ways that compound value per share over time. I want to thank the Ting team for building a valuable business, and for their continued care for customers through the transition."


**What the transaction means for Tucows**


Once the transaction closes, Tucows expects:


- **Less debt.** Approximately $301.5 million in principal amount of securitized notes will no longer be reported as Tucows debt. Tucows' remaining debt will consist principally of its syndicated credit facility, which had $184.4 million in principal outstanding at September 30, 2026.
- **Lower capital intensity.** Tucows will no longer fund fiber network construction and expansion in the markets being sold.
- **A clearer focus.** Tucows' financial profile will be led by its recurring-revenue platform businesses.


**2026 guidance**


Tucows' 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance, which excludes Ting, is unchanged from the outlook it provided with its third quarter 2026 results. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure; its definition is included in Tucows' quarterly earnings releases.


**Information for Ting customers**


Service, pricing, billing and support continue as they are, and Ting and Clearwave will coordinate the transition with continuity of service as the priority. Customers with questions can visit[https://tinginternet.com/updates](https://tinginternet.com/updates) .


**Advisors**


Rothschild & Co acted as exclusive financial advisor and Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP acted as legal counsel to Tucows.

**About Tucows**


Tucows helps connect more people to the benefit of internet access through domain services, communications service technology, and fiber-optic infrastructure. Tucows Domains ([https://tucowsdomains.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4824432-1&h=2869261319&u=https%3A%2F%2Ftucowsdomains.com%2F&a=https%3A%2F%2Ftucowsdomains.com) ) manages over 21 million domain names and millions of value-added services through a global reseller network of 32,000 web hosts and ISPs. Hover ([https://hover.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4824432-1&h=2214364224&u=https%3A%2F%2Fhover.com%2F&a=https%3A%2F%2Fhover.com) ) makes it easy for individuals and small businesses to manage their domain names and email addresses. Wavelo ([https://wavelo.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4824432-1&h=3986121075&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwavelo.com%2F&a=https%3A%2F%2Fwavelo.com) ) is a telecommunications software suite for service providers that simplifies the management of mobile and internet network access; provisioning, billing and subscription; developer tools; and more. Ting ([https://ting.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4824432-1&h=4258499279&u=https%3A%2F%2Fting.com%2Finternet&a=https%3A%2F%2Fting.com) ) delivers fixed fiber Internet access with outstanding customer support. More information can be found on Tucows' corporate website ([https://tucows.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4824432-1&h=4232040328&u=https%3A%2F%2Ftucows.com%2F&a=https%3A%2F%2Ftucows.com) ).
